result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend a coordinated Noto setup with separate faces per script, lang and dir tagging, bidi isolation for Latin stop names, and taller line-height per script. A covers more ground but drifts into line breaking, dark mode, truncation and pseudo-locale testing. It also contains doubtful claims: that Noto Sans Arabic's Latin glyphs match Noto Sans, and that word-break: auto-phrase works in Safari 17+. B stays closer to the typeface decisions, adds tabular figures for the departure times, and admits it hasn't checked licensing or file sizes, though it has a stray font-synthesis declaration outside any CSS rule. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers pick per-script Noto faces with language-tagged stacks. B is more complete: it covers size-adjust, per-language line height, digit choice, bidi isolation, and the platform trade-off between bundled and system Japanese fonts (Hiragino, Noto CJK), and its testing plan is stronger. A is more focused but thinner on platform gaps and has a stray `font-synthesis` declaration outside any rule. B overstates that Noto Sans Arabic's Latin glyphs match Noto Sans, and it strays into line breaking, truncation and dark mode, which costs it on focus.
